questions.q: What is the key difference between how an IDS and an IPS are deployed on a network?
options: An IPS sits inline in the traffic path and can block matching traffic; an IDS inspects a copy of traffic and can only alert
An IDS is always more expensive than an IPS
An IPS only works on wireless networks
There is no deployment difference; they are the same technology marketed differently
questions.explain: An IDS watches a passive copy of traffic and can only alert, while an IPS sits inline and can actually drop or block matching traffic.

questions.q: How does an IDS typically receive the traffic it inspects?
options: IDS sensors generate their own synthetic traffic to test the network
Through a SPAN port or network tap that sends it a copy of the traffic
By intercepting and holding every packet before forwarding it
Only through manually uploaded log files
questions.explain: A switch is configured to mirror traffic to the IDS through a SPAN port or tap, so the IDS sees a copy out of band.

questions.q: Why can't an IDS stop an attack that it detects?
options: An IDS can always stop an attack; this is a common misconception
IDS sensors run slower than the network itself
It only sees a copy of the traffic after the original packet has already reached its destination
IDS sensors are not allowed to send alerts
questions.explain: By the time the IDS inspects the mirrored copy, the original packet was already delivered — there's nothing left to block.

questions.q: What is the main risk of running a detection rule in IPS (blocking) mode?
options: IPS sensors require a SPAN port to function
IPS mode has no risk compared to IDS mode
IPS mode cannot generate any alerts at all
A false positive doesn't just raise a noisy alert — it blocks real traffic and can cause an outage
questions.explain: Because the IPS sits inline, a misfiring rule blocks legitimate traffic outright, which can take down a real business process.

questions.q: Why do SOC teams often deploy a brand-new detection rule in IDS mode before switching it to IPS mode?
options: To confirm the rule's false-positive rate is low against real traffic before trusting it to block anything
Because IPS mode cannot be configured until the rule is a year old
There is no reason — most teams start directly in IPS mode
Because IDS mode is required by law for all new rules
questions.explain: Running a new rule in IDS mode first lets a team tune it and prove it's reliable before letting it actually block traffic.
